Content covers: Rabbi Yehuda's ruling that only the incense (not the fire-pan) required its own lottery, with the two-priest incense-and-coal mechanics and both proposed reasons (rarity, enrichment) for why the incense alone needed a separate lottery despite being paired with the fire-pan; the open question of whether the slaughterer or the blood-tosser receives the blood, resolved from Ben Katin's twelve-spout laver (proving thirteen priests, hence the tosser receives) and independently confirmed from the Tamid mishnah's own phrasing; Ben Azzai's, Rabbi Yosei's, Rabbi Akiva's, and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili's four competing orderings for dismembering and carrying the daily-offering's limbs (by the order the animal walked, was flayed, was dismembered, and was ranked by quality respectively); the verse-based challenge that the thigh is the finest cut versus fat being the finest, resolved by animal condition (lean versus fatty); and Rava's resolution that both the mishnah's own tanna and Rabbi Yosei actually agree on ranking by fat-quality, merely applying it via different metrics (limb size versus fat quantity), closing into the second scriptural mention of fat, continuing onto 26a.
